subject: Fwd: BrightWave - A/B promptset acceptance and rollback criteria
messages:
From: Sara Lopez <sara@brightwave.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarification on A/B acceptance for prompt tuning

Marissa —

Thanks again for the call this morning. We ran the initial A/B with your suggested prompt augmentations and saw a small but consistent quality delta on our billing-related intents. High-level:

- Baseline (A) vs Variant (B): B reduces hallucination on product descriptions but decreases correct-entity extraction for billing flows from 94.6% -> 92.1%.
- This shows up in the automated scoring (intent accuracy) and a handful of human-eval cases (attached samples).

Our ask: we need clear acceptance criteria for the canary so we can sign off on a rollout. Specifically:
1) What absolute/relative drop in intent accuracy is acceptable before we block?
2) Do you have a recommended set of fallback/rollback triggers (metric thresholds + user-visible error signals)?
3) Example canary size & time window that Redwood recommends for accounts like ours (heavy billing traffic, bursty).

I've attached the sample-fail-cases.jsonl and a spreadsheet with our current eval scoring. Happy to hop on a call if useful.

— Sara
Senior Product Manager
BrightWave

Attachments: BW-eval-acceptance-criteria.xlsx (spreadsheet), sample-fail-cases.jsonl (jsonl)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: 
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: BrightWave - A/B promptset acceptance and rollback criteria

Forwarding Sara's note — BrightWave hit a small but material drop on billing intent accuracy when testing the prompt augment. They want firm acceptance criteria and a canary plan before we proceed with a wide rollout.

Actions I'm proposing:
- Karthik: define the metric definitions (intent accuracy, confusion matrix boundaries) and a strict vs lenient threshold set. We need both an automated gating rule and a human-review window.
- Grace: product-side escalation policy — if intent accuracy drop > X absolute points OR user-impacting errors appear, who makes the call and what messaging goes to the customer?
- Jonas: CS coordination and proposed canary cadence with the account. Also please draft the customer-facing rollback playbook.
- Priyom: make sure our eval infra can produce the per-traffic-segment signal (billing vs non-billing) and a canary dashboard we can hand to the account.

I'm attaching a quick skeleton for an acceptance matrix and a canary checklist (see attachments). Can you each reply with concrete thresholds and an owner by EOD Monday?

Marissa Cole
Director, Product Ops — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachments: BW-eval-acceptance-criteria.xlsx, bw-canary-plan.md

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 06 Dec 2026 07:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: BrightWave - A/B promptset acceptance and rollback criteria

Quick notes from infra/metrics perspective:

1) Metric defs:
   - Intent accuracy: weighted macro over billing intent set (per-customer weighted by traffic fraction).
   - Hallucination rate: % of responses with extraneous entities as judged by our annotation spec.

2) Recommended gating thresholds (initial proposal):
   - Absolute intent accuracy drop <= 1.0 percentage point (preferred);
   - Hard stop if drop > 2.0 percentage points OR hallucination delta > 1.5 pp;
   - Soft alert if drop between 1.0 - 2.0 pp: require human triage and 24h hold.

3) Canary sizing:
   - Start with 1% of production traffic for 48 hours (min 10k requests), then 5% for 72 hours if stable.
   - Instrument per-traffic-segment metrics (billing vs misc) and require no rollback triggers in any top-3 segments.

I'll produce a short doc with exact SQL/queries for the metrics and add them to the BW drive link. Priyom — I need the per-segment hooks; can you confirm feasibility?

— Karthik
Lead, Eval Instrumentation

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 06 Dec 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: BrightWave - A/B promptset acceptance and rollback criteria

Thanks — concise and helpful. A couple of product/CS process points: 

- Decision authority: Product Ops (Marissa) owns the acceptance sign-off for canaries under $X ARR; anything above that escalates to Revenue Ops + Head of Product. Let's mark BrightWave as 'escalate' given their revenue profile.
- Customer communication: if we hit a soft alert, CS crafts a status note and a short FAQ; if we hit hard stop we schedule a war room within 1 hour and roll back variant B.
- External transparency: recommend we share the canary dashboard read-only link with BrightWave after week 1 so their PMs can see the signal.

I'll add the language for the customer-facing rollback playbook and a short decision rubric to the bw-canary-plan.md attachment. Timeline: I can have the rubric + FAQ by Monday noon PT.

— Grace
Sr. Product Manager, Reliability
